name: Surfside Fish House
notes: surfsidefishhouse.com 403s a direct curl/plain fetch (custom WAF), so the PDFs were pulled via WebFetch (which returns the actual binary) and read with pdftotext -raw. The in-house PDF renders as parallel name-block/price-block columns rather than inline pairs; sequence-order pairing was cross-checked against pdftotext -layout output for every section and matched exactly (verified section by section: starters, soups, salads, poke bowls, entrees, prepared-fish choices, tacos, burritos, sandwiches, sides, drinks, oysters). Happy Hour is a genuine separate dine-in-only menu (stated 'DINE-IN ONLY') with lower prices on overlapping items - kept as daypart variants, not deduped. Kids menu (kidsmenu.jpg) read directly off the image, flat $5.99 per item including a fountain soda. Cup/bowl soup pricing and oyster tiered pricing split into separate rows to keep one price per row. Sections reached: starters, soups, salads, poke bowls, oysters, entrees, prepared fish, full tacos, a la carte tacos, burritos, sandwiches, sides, non-alcoholic drinks, happy hour, kids menu. Not reached: full bar/wine/beer list referenced as 'full drink menu' (adjunct, not priced on this PDF).

name: VYBZ Kitchen & Lounge
notes: vybzsd.com (the work-list URL) is a hijacked domain — curl -sL follows a redirect chain to an unrelated Indonesian gambling/slots site ('SLOT777... Situs Slot88'). The restaurant's real current site is vybzsandiego.com (found via WebSearch, corroborated by Yelp/Tripadvisor/gaslamp.org all giving the same 840 5th Ave address), but its SpotHopper-powered /food-menu page server-renders only an explicit empty-state message ('We are updating our menu. Please stay tuned.') — confirmed genuinely empty, not gated, by reading the rendered HTML directly (food_menu_v2 section, empty-content-message block). Fell back to the DoorDash marketplace listing, which server-renders full schema.org Menu/MenuItem JSON-LD (29 items across 6 sections: Starters, Salads/Soup, Small Plates, Burgers, Fire Oven Pizzas, Tacos/Burros/Papas). Ran the markup-divisor test (1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25) against all 29 prices — no consistent divisor lands them on round numbers, so this reads as organic whole-dollar pricing rather than a uniform delivery markup. No second priced source was reachable to cross-check (own site menu is empty), so this stays medium per the tier-3 DoorDash-marketplace ceiling. Sections reached: Starters, Salads/Soup, Small Plates, Burgers, Pizzas, Tacos/Burros/Papas. Not reached: any dedicated entrees/mains section (may not exist for a lounge menu) and the full bar/cocktail list (adjunct).

name: The Bon Cha
notes: theboncha.com is a Wix site whose homepage and every path tried (/menu, /order, /food-menu, /ordering) all return the identical client-routed SPA shell (title always 'HOME | Theboncha') with no data-hook="item.name"/"item.price" spans anywhere and no ordering-platform embed found in the HTML — the site itself carries no readable menu. Fell back to the DoorDash marketplace listing (address confirmed streetAddress '330 G Street', matching the work list exactly), which server-renders full schema.org Menu/MenuItem JSON-LD. The 'Most Ordered' carousel (12 items) is a pure duplicate sample of items that also appear, at matching prices, in the proper categories below — dropped per the dedupe rule since nothing in it is unique. Markup-divisor test (1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25) on all 51 remaining prices found no consistent divisor landing them on round numbers; the .50/.00 pattern reads as this business's normal boba/coffee pricing, not a uniform delivery markup. No second priced source was reachable to cross-check, so this stays medium per the tier-3 DoorDash-marketplace ceiling. Sections reached: Milk Teas, Smoothies, Flavored Teas, Espresso/Latte/Mocha, Acai Bowls, Cookies & Desserts. Not reached: none apparent on the DoorDash storefront beyond these.
